companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The software and personal computer maker reported a record year in 2022 as full-year revenue reached $102.3 billion, up 1% from 2021.

  • Full-year operating income rose 24% year over year as Dell launched new products like its new PowerEdge servers and the world’s first 6K resolution monitor.

  • Dell reported its record year in 2022 despite a rough fourth quarter: Its computer shipments fell 37%, a decline that was far steeper than those recorded at rivals Lenovo, HP, and Apple in the same period.

  • Dell started 2023 on a sour note: Amid lower PC demand and uncertain market conditions, the company announced it would cut about 5% of its workforce in February.

“What I appreciate about Dell is the ability to do challenging, meaningful work every day with some of the brightest, most talented people in our industry. companyRankingLists.itemDescription: More remote work meant more demand for Dell Technologies’ desktops and laptops in 2021, and revenue grew 13.6% to $106 billion. In November 2021, Dell announced that it had completed the sale of its majority stake in cloud-computing software company VMware, in a deal that returned about $12 billion to Dell shareholders and helped Dell pay down some of its substantial debt load.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Sales at Dell Technologies inched up 2% year over year to $94.2 billion, adding to the tech behemoth’s slow-and-steady rise since going public three years ago. Demand for the company’s personal computers, laptops, and desktop monitors swelled as COVID-19 forced people to work remotely. Revenue for the consumer electronics division rose 5% year over year to $48.4 billion, amounting to more than half of the company’s total business. In April, Dell said it would spin out VMware, the enterprise software firm that Dell acquired as part of its 2015 acquisition of EMC. The move is expected to generate up to $9.7 billion for Dell, key to paying down outstanding debt.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Dell's second year after returning as a publicly traded company finished with overall sales (for the fiscal year ending Jan. 31) up a modest 2%, to $92.2 billion. The technology conglomerate still faces big challenges selling data center hardware like servers and storage devices, as more businesses buy on-demand cloud computing resources from other tech giants. But its VMware enterprise software unit is growing fast, with annual sales up 12% year-over-year, to $10.9 billion. No wonder Dell CEO Michael Dell referred to VMware as the “crown jewel” of the EMC Federation, the enterprise hardware giant Dell bought in 2016.
